outcome: Composite of neonatal morbidity and mortality

Large for gestational age at birth
cohort: The study included data from 9534 nulliparous women recruited in the first trimester at 8 US clinical centers between 2010 and 2014, with estimated fetal weight obtained from ultrasounds.
finding: Despite classifying different proportions of fetuses as fetal growth restriction or estimated fetal weight>90, all six population-based fetal growth standards performed similarly in predicting perinatal morbidity and mortality.
birth_weight: N/A (study focused on classifications of fetal weight relative to gestational age, such as small for gestational age and large for gestational age, rather than a specific birth weight range)
gest_age: Fetal growth standards were applied to estimated fetal weight measurements obtained at 16-21 and 22-29 weeks of gestation.
